newsitem.title: KAZAKHSTAN: Kazakhstan to narrow tender for giant Uzen oilfiel.
newsitem.headline: Kazakhstan to narrow tender for giant Uzen oilfiel.

text.p: A Kazakh privatisation official said on Tuesday that one of three participants in a tender for the former Soviet republic's giant Uzen oilfield would be eliminated from the competition in the next week.

"We are proposing steps towards finding a definite winner, with the next step being to eliminate the weakest (competitor), which will happen in the next week," Birzhan Madiev, chairman of the tender commission at Kazakhstan's state property committee, told a news conference.
Amoco Corp of the United States, the China National Petroleum Corp and Malaysia's state oil firm Petronas are the three companies competing in the tender, which was announced in February 1996.
They had been asked by the government to improve their offers, and all three submitted new bids on Tuesday.

Officials say the Uzenmunaigaz enterprise, located in southwest Kazakhstan near the Caspian Sea, is sitting on estimated oil reserves of 852 million tonnes -- the second largest in the country after the massive Tengiz oil field.
Production at Uzenmunaigaz peaked in 1975 at 16 million tonnes (320,000 barrels per day), but slipped to a meagre 2.8 million tonnes (56,000 bpd) last year.
The government, which says the enterprise needs around $1.2 billion in investment, aims to boost output with foreign investment to about seven million tonnes (140,000 bpd) annually.
Madiev would not be drawn on sums being negotiated with the three companies. "The market will fix the price," he said.
The World Bank has lent the enterprise $108 million to rehabilitate its ageing Soviet-era wells.
